subject: Post-call recap: efficiency anchors, budget & pilot checkpoints
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: efficiency anchors, budget & pilot checkpoints

Hi Elena —

Thanks for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and the pilot proposal so we’re aligned on goals, constraints, and next steps. I kept this tight so you can paste into procurement if helpful.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Peak inference spend during end-of-day reconciliation spikes 20–30x and is the primary budget pain.
- Two main workloads: (1) real-time fraud scoring (P95 latency target ~350ms) and (2) customer summary generation (higher token counts, less strict latency).
- Budget constraint: stated comfortable runway ~ $25k/month for inference during pilot qualification; procurement needs an ROI one-pager and an estimated TCO.
- Success metrics: maintain fraud P95 under 400ms, keep average cost-per-transaction under $0.10, and demonstrate >= 30% unit-cost reduction vs current provider during the pilot window.

Initial economic assumptions (ballpark for sizing the pilot)
- Baseline (from your notes): ~20M tokens/month across both workloads (approx).
- Example current spend estimate (you mentioned your vendor): $0.0008/token => ~$16k/month baseline (needs verification).
- Redwood levers we proposed: batching (continuous micro-batching for scoring), prefix/KV caching for repeated prompting in summaries, and mixed-precision / 4-bit quantization variants for background generation.
- Expected illustrative impact: batching ~25–35% fewer compute tokens (depending on arrival patterns); caching ~15–25% reduction on repeat prompt content; quantization ~30–45% lower compute cost for compatible models. These multiply, not add — final will depend on trace.

Pilot proposal (6 weeks) — low-friction, measurable
- Scope: run on a representative subset: 20% production traffic mirrored to Redwood Dedicated sandbox (scoring + summaries).
- Timeline: 1 week setup + 4 weeks trace + 1 week analysis and readout.
- Deliverables: TCO/ROI one-pager, a per-route token and latency dashboard, a runbook with recommended batching/cache params, and a short ops checklist for production rollout.
- Ask from Mintline (what we need to proceed): recent 2–3 weeks of anonymized request logs (timestamps, route, prompt length, response length), SLO constraints per route, and a PO or approval to run the sandbox mirror. We can accept a narrow legal/MOU for the sandbox — not a full MSA to start.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-scope-tco.pdf (one-pager), mintline-trace-template.xlsx (log template) — attached for your procurement/team.

Next steps
1) If this aligns, can you confirm procurement’s preferred intake (one-pager + PO vs SOW)?
2) Rishi to run a quick high-level savings calc once we have a week of traces (2–3 business days after logs).
3) Schedule the decision/approval review — suggested window: Aug 13–15.

Thanks again — I’ll keep this thread as the single source for pilot artifacts.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[jasmine@redwood.com]

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the clear recap — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wants. A few clarifying points from my side before I route to legal & procurement:

- Baseline check: the $0.0008/token ballpark is what we currently pay on average, but that includes a mix of cheap embedding calls and expensive long-form generations. I’ll try to split that out when I send logs.
- Procurement timeline: historically 6–8 weeks if we need a contract amendment. For a sandbox mirror + MOU we can sometimes accelerate to 2–3 weeks if the ROI is clear.
- SLA / data residency: for scoring we need to confirm that traces and mirrored requests remain within us-west-2 and are purged after the pilot unless we agree otherwise.

What procurement needs from Redwood (one-pager items)
1) Estimated monthly spend under the pilot (using your proposed levers) with a high/likely/low band.
2) A short list of required legal terms for the sandbox (data handling + deletion, IP, liability cap).
3) A clear success criteria line for us to sign-off (we like the 30% unit-cost reduction target but want a concrete measurement approach).

I’ll loop in procurement on this thread — @procurement: please advise required intake docs.

Agree on Aug 13 for a decision sync; can we do the morning slot (08:30–10:00 PT)?

Best,

Hi Elena — quick technical addendum on how we’d measure and an illustrative savings calc so procurement has a starting point.

Measurement approach (what we’ll compute from traces)
- Request-level fields we need (or approximate): arrival timestamp, route id, prompt token count, response token count, response latency, and a small hash of prompt template to group similar prompts. The trace template attached in Jasmine’s note is what we prefer.
- We’ll simulate continuous micro-batching using your arrival patterns to estimate effective token reductions (batching reduces per-request overhead and can reduce redundant decoder token work).
- Caching: for conversational summaries we’ll measure identical-prefix frequency and estimate KV cache hit rates.

Illustrative savings (simple example — will refine on real traces)
- Baseline: 20M tokens/month * $0.0008/token = $16,000/month compute cost (example).
- If batching reduces effective compute tokens by 30% => 14M tokens => $11,200/month.
- If caching reduces that remaining workload by 20% on the summary route => 11.2M effective tokens => $8,960/month.
- If we can also run quantized variants for the background generation portion that accounts for ~40% of tokens and it reduces compute cost by 40% on that slice => additional ~ $1,800 savings estimated.
- Combined illustrative result => total of roughly $6k–$7k/month versus baseline in this toy calc (~40% overall reduction).

Important caveats
- These effects are multiplicative and route-dependent. For scoring routes with strict latency targets we may only apply batching at micro-batch sizes that preserve P95.
- Quantization may not be appropriate for every model / prompt shape; we’ll profile quality vs perf on your sample prompts.
- Real savings require representative arrival patterns — hence the short 4-week mirrored trace.

Operational asks from us
- A single week of request headers/lengths to run an initial sim (we don’t need PII).
- SLA tolerance per route (P95 thresholds).
- Point person for infra/ELB routing for the mirror — we’ll keep traffic mirrored (read-only) and never touch production writes.

If procurement wants, I can draft a short technical appendix for the one-pager that explains the assumptions and the simulation method.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
